content.name: Content
content.value: This strand focuses on students applying the seven transferable skills in language and literacy contexts, developing digital media literacy skills, applying language and literacy learning in other contexts, and engaging with texts that foster understanding of diverse identities, experiences, perspectives, histories, and contributions. In all grades of the language program, the learning related to this strand takes place in the context of learning related to Strand B, Foundations of Language; Strand C, Comprehension: Understanding and Responding to Texts; and Strand D, Composition: Expressing Ideas and Creating Texts. Strand A should be assessed and evaluated within these contexts.

content.name: Content
content.value: For an elaboration of the mandatory learning associated with specific expectations, see the “More Details” sections below. For an at-a-glance view of this learning across grades, see Appendix A: Language Foundations Continuum for Reading and Writing, Kindergarten–Grade 4.

title.name: Title
title.value: Indigenous Context of Various Text Forms

content.name: Content
content.value: read, listen to, and view various forms of texts by diverse First Nations, Métis, and Inuit creators and demonstrate understanding of various aspects of First Nations, Métis, and Inuit histories, cultures, relationships, communities, groups, nations, and lived experiences

title.name: Title
title.value: Summarizing: Identifying Relevant Information and Drawing Conclusions

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the main idea in a simple text, and relate important details in sequence

content.name: Content
content.value: describe how strategies, such as visualizing, making predictions, and connecting to their experiences, have helped them comprehend various texts

content.name: Content
content.value: identify thinking skills that have helped them analyze and better understand various texts

content.name: Content
content.value: edit draft texts to improve accuracy and style, checking for errors in spelling, punctuation, grammar, and text conventions, and proofread edited texts to make corrections

content.name: Content
content.value: <object type="application/kenticocloud" data-type="item" data-rel="link" data-codename="enl1w___frl1w___a___note__copy_"></object>

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of how the seven transferable skills (critical thinking and problem solving; innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurship; self-directed learning; collaboration; communication; global citizenship and sustainability; and digital literacy) are used in various language and literacy contexts

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate and apply the knowledge and skills needed to interact safely and responsibly in online environments, use digital and media tools to construct knowledge, and demonstrate learning as critical consumers and creators of media

title.name: Title
title.value: First Nations, Métis, and Inuit Perspectives and Ways of Knowing

content.name: Content
content.value: identify themes explored in First Nations, Métis, and Inuit cultures to demonstrate an understanding of the varied identities, perspectives, relationships, legacies, truths, and ways of knowing, being, and doing

content.name: Content
content.value: use effective listening skills, including asking questions to clarify information and ideas, in formal and informal contexts and for various purposes, including in small- and large-group conversations and various classroom activities

content.name: Content
content.value: select and use a variety of listening strategies before, during, and after listening to comprehend information communicated orally and non-verbally, recognize when a message is difficult to understand, and develop an appropriate response

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the purpose and audience for speaking in formal and informal contexts, and use appropriate speaking strategies, including establishing a rapport with the audience, to communicate clearly and coherently

title.name: Title
title.value: Word-Level Reading and Spelling: Using Phonics Knowledge

content.name: Content
content.value: use consolidated phonics knowledge, including phonemic blending to read words and set for variability to correct approximations, and phonemic segmentation to spell phonetically regular monosyllabic and multisyllabic words, in isolation and various text contexts

title.name: Title
title.value: Word-Level Reading and Spelling: Using Orthographic Knowledge

content.name: Content
content.value: use consolidated orthographic knowledge, including position-based tendencies, to make a spelling choice or accurately pronounce a word when reading

title.name: Title
title.value: Word-Level Reading and Spelling: Using Morphological Knowledge

content.name: Content
content.value: use developing knowledge of the meanings of words and morphemes (i.e., bases, prefixes, and suffixes) to read and spell words

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of a variety of words, acquire and use explicitly taught vocabulary in various contexts, including other subject areas, and use morphological knowledge to analyze and understand new words in context

title.name: Title
title.value: Reading Fluency: Accuracy, Rate, and Prosody

content.name: Content
content.value: read words, complex sentences, and paragraphs in a variety of texts fluently, with accuracy and appropriate pacing to support comprehension, and read aloud using varied expression and intonation according to the purpose of reading

content.name: Content
content.value: identify and construct various sentence types and forms, including simple sentences, compound sentences, and complex sentences containing adverbial clauses

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the functions of parts of speech in sentences, including possessive nouns, linking verbs and the progressive tense, interrogative adjectives and adverbs, and prepositions and interjections, and use this knowledge to support comprehension and communicate meaning clearly

content.name: Content
content.value: use their understanding of the meaning and function of capitalization and punctuation to communicate meaning clearly, including the use of capital letters in dialogue and for words in titles, commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and direct quotations from texts within sentences, and apostrophes to indicate contractions

title.name: Title
title.value: Comprehension: Understanding and Responding to Texts

content.name: Content
content.value: apply foundational knowledge and skills to understand a variety of texts, including digital and media texts, by creators with diverse identities, perspectives, and experience, and demonstrate an understanding of the patterns, features, and elements of style associated with various text forms and genres

title.name: Title
title.value: Using Foundational Knowledge and Skills to Comprehend Texts

content.name: Content
content.value: read and comprehend various texts, using knowledge of words, grammar, cohesive ties, sentence structures, and background knowledge

content.name: Content
content.value: identify and describe some characteristics of literary and informational text forms and their associated genres

content.name: Content
content.value: identify some text patterns, such as order of importance and cause and effect, and text features, such as headings and an index, associated with various text forms, and explain how they help readers, listeners, and viewers understand the meaning

content.name: Content
content.value: apply comprehension strategies before, during, and after reading, listening to, and viewing a variety of texts, including digital and media texts, by creators with diverse identities, perspectives, and experience, in order to understand and clarify the meaning of texts

content.name: Content
content.value: activate prior knowledge, including knowledge gained from personal and text experiences, that they can use to make connections and understand the topic and form of new texts

title.name: Title
title.value: Prereading: Identifying the Purpose for Reading, Listening, and Viewing

content.name: Content
content.value: identify specific purposes for engaging with texts, including learning facts or information, or to gain insight or new perspectives

title.name: Title
title.value: Monitoring of Understanding: Making and Confirming Predictions

content.name: Content
content.value: make predictions using background knowledge, text features, and evidence from the text, and adjust their understanding based on new information

title.name: Title
title.value: Monitoring of Understanding: Ongoing Comprehension Check

content.name: Content
content.value: use strategies such as rereading, visualizing, and asking questions, to monitor and confirm their understanding of various texts

content.name: Content
content.value: apply critical thinking skills to deepen understanding of texts, and analyze how various perspectives and topics are communicated and addressed in a variety of texts, including digital, media, and cultural texts

content.name: Content
content.value: identify literary devices, including metaphor and assonance, and describe how they help communicate meaning

content.name: Content
content.value: make inferences using stated and implied information and ideas to understand texts

content.name: Content
content.value: analyze various texts, including literary and informational texts, by identifying main and supporting ideas, sequencing information, and comparing and contrasting elements

content.name: Content
content.value: identify some cultural elements represented in various texts, including symbols, language, and values, and pose questions and share ideas about how these elements contribute to the meaning

content.name: Content
content.value: identify explicit and implicit perspectives communicated in texts, providing evidence, and explain how these perspectives could influence an audience

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate a personal voice in their texts, using descriptive words and sentence patterns to express their thoughts, feelings, and opinions about the topic

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the point of view, including first person or third person, used in their texts

content.name: Content
content.value: make simple revisions to draft texts, including replacing words and adding sentences, to improve content and clarity, using feedback from others

title.name: Title
title.value: Language Foundations for Reading and Writing

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of foundational language knowledge and skills, and apply this understanding when reading and writing

title.name: Title
title.value: Language Conventions for Reading and Writing

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of sentence structure, grammar, cohesive ties, and capitalization and punctuation, and apply this knowledge when reading and writing sentences, paragraphs, and a variety of texts

content.name: Content
content.value: identify how transferable skills can be used to support communication in various cultural, social, linguistic, and domain-specific contexts, and apply them when reading, listening to, viewing, and creating texts of various forms

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of how transferable skills help them to express their voice and be engaged in their learning

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of their rights and responsibilities when interacting online with appropriate permission, and make decisions that contribute positively to the development of their digital identity and those of their communities

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of how to navigate online environments safely, manage their privacy, and interact in a way that supports their well-being and that of others, including seeking appropriate permission

content.name: Content
content.value: gather, evaluate, and use information, considering various perspectives, to construct knowledge and demonstrate learning

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the forms, conventions, and techniques of digital and media texts, and apply this understanding when analyzing texts

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the interrelationships between the form, message, and context of a text, the audience, and the creator

content.name: Content
content.value: use digital and media tools to support stages of the design process and to develop creative solutions to authentic, real-world problems

content.name: Content
content.value: communicate and collaborate with various communities in a safe, respectful, responsible, and inclusive manner when using online platforms and environments, including digital and media tools, and demonstrate cultural awareness with members of the community

content.name: Content
content.value: apply the knowledge and skills developed in this grade to support learning in various subject areas and identify some ways this learning can be used in everyday life

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the contributions, lived experiences, and perspectives of a diversity of individuals and communities, including those in Canada, by exploring the concepts of identity, self, and sense of belonging in culturally responsive and relevant texts

content.name: Content
content.value: identify and use oral and non-verbal communication strategies, including expression, gestures, and body language, and demonstrate an understanding of how these strategies can contribute to the meaning being conveyed

title.name: Title
title.value: Word Choice, Syntax, and Grammar in Oral Communication

content.name: Content
content.value: use appropriate word choice, including new vocabulary, grammar, and cohesive sentences when speaking and communicating ideas in various contexts, to support audience comprehension

content.name: Content
content.value: describe ways in which images, graphics, and visual design are used in a given text, and demonstrate an understanding of their purpose and connection to the content of the text

content.name: Content
content.value: identify some elements of style in texts, including voice, word choice, word patterns, and sentence structure, and explain how they help communicate meaning

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the narrator’s point of view, including first person or third person, in a variety of texts, and suggest alternative points of view to tell each story

content.name: Content
content.value: identify connections between ideas expressed in texts and their knowledges and lived experiences, the ideas in other texts, and the world around them

content.name: Content
content.value: describe personal thoughts and feelings about ideas presented in texts, such as ideas about diversity, inclusion, and accessibility

content.name: Content
content.value: identify some ways in which texts created by First Nations, Métis, and Inuit individuals, communities, groups, or nations communicate about historical periods, cultural experiences, and events, and how they relate to current lived experiences

title.name: Title
title.value: Composition: Expressing Ideas and Creating Texts

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the topic, purpose, and audience for various texts they plan to create, and describe how the chosen text form and genre will help communicate their intended meaning

content.name: Content
content.value: generate and develop ideas about given and chosen topics, using various strategies, and drawing on various resources, including their own lived experiences, and learning from other subject areas

content.name: Content
content.value: gather information and content relevant to a topic, using three or more sources

content.name: Content
content.value: sort and sequence ideas and information, using appropriate strategies and tools, taking into account the text form and genre to be used

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the strategies that helped them develop ideas for texts and organize content

content.name: Content
content.value: plan, develop ideas, gather information, and organize content for creating texts of various forms, including digital and media texts, on a variety of topics

content.name: Content
content.value: draft short texts of various forms and genres, including narrative, persuasive, and informational texts, using a variety of media, tools, and strategies

content.name: Content
content.value: begin to write in cursive, forming letters with appropriate formation patterns, size, placement, and spacing

content.name: Content
content.value: apply knowledge and understanding of various text forms and genres to create, revise, edit, and proofread their own texts, using a variety of media, tools, and strategies, and reflect critically on created texts

content.name: Content
content.value: produce final texts using simple techniques, to achieve the intended effect

content.name: Content
content.value: present the texts they have created using appropriate strategies, including by reading aloud with expression

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the strategies that helped them present and communicate their message, and explain how they helped them improve as a text creator

content.name: Content
content.value: select suitable and effective media, techniques, and tools to publish and present final texts, and critically analyze how well the texts address various topics

content.name: Content
content.value: apply language and literacy skills in cross-curricular and integrated learning, and demonstrate an understanding of, and make connections to, diverse voices, experiences, perspectives, histories, and contributions, including those of First Nations, Métis, and Inuit individuals, communities, groups, and nations

content.name: Content
content.value: apply listening, speaking, and non-verbal communication skills and strategies to understand and communicate meaning in formal and informal contexts and for various purposes and audiences
